early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings ('bullseye' pattern) on older lower leaves, leaf yellowing (chlorosis) around lesions.

severity_classification.mild: Small isolated lesions (<5mm) on bottom leaves only
severity_classification.moderate: Multiple concentric lesions, lower leaves turning yellow, spreading to mid-canopy
severity_classification.severe: Extensive defoliation, stem lesions, canopy loss >40%

treatments.application_method: Precision foliar misting targeting lower canopy lesions
treatments.safety_notes: Wear respirator & nitrile gloves. 48-hour re-entry interval. Toxic to aquatic life.
treatments.source: USDA-ARS Vegetable Crop Pathology & ICAR Plant Protection Handbook

treatments.application_method: Targeted wetting of affected leaves at early symptom stage
treatments.safety_notes: Organic certified. Safe for beneficial pollinators if sprayed late evening.
treatments.source: OMRI Listed Organic Agriculture Materials Review

late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems with white fungal fuzz on leaf undersides under humid conditions.

severity_classification.mild: Water-soaked irregular spots on edge of leaf tips
severity_classification.moderate: Fast-expanding grey-green lesions with white fungal growth on undersides
severity_classification.severe: Systemic collapse, blackened stems, rotting fruit

treatments.application_method: High-pressure fine cone nozzle spray coating leaf undersides
treatments.safety_notes: High potency. Mandatory PPE. 7-day harvest interval.
treatments.source: FAO Integrated Pest Management Guidelines for Tomato

bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small (1-3mm) circular dark brown/black spots on leaves surrounded by a yellow halo, greasy appearance on underside.

severity_classification.mild: Few scattered dark speckles (<10 per leaf)
severity_classification.moderate: Dense speckling, chlorosis, ragged hole formation
severity_classification.severe: Extensive leaf scorch and premature drop

treatments.safety_notes: Avoid spraying when foliage is wet. Rotate modes of action to prevent resistance.
treatments.source: Cornell Cooperative Extension Disease Management Sheet

septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with grey centers and dark margins; tiny dark pycnidia specks inside spots.

severity_classification.mild: Scattered spots on lowest older leaves
severity_classification.severe: Upward progression, complete defoliation of lower two-thirds

treatments.application_method: Precision downward spray directly onto diseased leaf area
treatments.safety_notes: Full protective suit and respirator. Avoid non-target drift.

healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage, normal turgor, no visible lesions, chlorosis or necrotic tissue.

nitrogen_deficiency.guidance: Symptom appears related to Nitrogen deficiency rather than fungal blight. Recommended action: Soil side-dressing or fertigation with nitrogen-rich amendment. Do NOT apply foliar fungicides.

soil_drought_stress.guidance: Critically low soil moisture detected (drought stress). Applying chemical sprays during severe water stress can cause chemical leaf burn. Recommended action: Irrigate first.

high_humidity_blight_risk.guidance: High temperature-humidity disease window active. Conditions favor spore germination and rapid spread.
